items.headline: Bellingham's Extra-Time Heroics Send England to Semifinals
items.body: England secured a hard-fought 2-1 extra-time victory over Norway in a captivating Quarterfinal clash. Jude Bellingham emerged as the hero, scoring both goals for the Three Lions, including the decisive winner in the 93rd minute. Norway's Andreas Schjelderup had initially opened the scoring, but England's resilience proved too much.

metadata.venue: Hard Rock Stadium, Miami Gardens, Florida, USA

items.headline: Tactical Battle of Titans: Tuchel's Substitutions Pay Off
items.body: The match was a tactical chess match, with Norway's early lead forcing England to adapt. Gareth Southgate's (or Thomas Tuchel's, as per some reports) strategic substitutions, including Bukayo Saka and Eberechi Eze, injected fresh attacking impetus in the second half and extra time. Norway's disciplined defense and counter-attacking threat, led by Erling Haaland, tested England throughout the 120 minutes.

items.headline: Key Moments: VAR Decisions and Near Misses Define Contest
items.body: Critical moments included Andreas Schjelderup's opening goal for Norway in the 36th minute and Jude Bellingham's equalizer just before halftime, assisted by Anthony Gordon. Both teams had goals disallowed by VAR, with Harry Kane's effort ruled offside and Torbjorn Heggem's strike chalked off due to a foul in the build-up. Kristoffer Ajer also hit the post in the 76th minute, highlighting the fine margins of the game.

items.headline: Bellingham's Brilliance Leads England to Victory
items.body: Jude Bellingham delivered a standout individual performance, scoring both of England's goals. His equalizer in first-half stoppage time provided crucial momentum, and his 93rd-minute winner showcased his composure and clinical finishing under immense pressure. Erling Haaland also had a memorable run in the tournament, leading the Golden Boot race with seven goals.

items.headline: England's Resilient Form Continues to Impress
items.body: England's victory against Norway, following a thrilling 3-2 win over Mexico in the Round of 16, demonstrates their ability to grind out results under pressure. The team has shown resilience and tactical flexibility, adapting to various challenges throughout the tournament. Their path to the semifinals has been marked by crucial goals from key players like Harry Kane and Jude Bellingham.

items.headline: Injury Watch: No Major Concerns Reported for England
items.body: No significant new injury concerns have been reported for the England squad following their extra-time battle against Norway. Manager Gareth Southgate (or Thomas Tuchel) will be keen to ensure his squad recovers fully ahead of the demanding semifinal fixture. Declan Rice was reportedly recovering from a pre-match illness but played.

items.headline: France vs. Spain: A Blockbuster Semifinal Confirmed
items.body: The first semifinal is set to be a highly anticipated clash between European giants France and Spain. France secured their spot by defeating Morocco, while Spain overcame Belgium in their Quarterfinal match. This matchup features two of the top-ranked teams in FIFA's live rankings.

items.headline: Head-to-Head History Favors Spain in Recent Encounters
items.body: Recent history between France and Spain favors La Roja, with Spain coming out on top in their Euro 2024 semifinal and 2025 Nations League encounters. Lamine Yamal, in particular, has been a key figure in Spain's recent successes against France. This history adds an intriguing layer to their upcoming World Cup semifinal.

items.headline: Tactical Expectations: High-Stakes European Showdown
items.body: Expect a high-intensity tactical battle between France and Spain, with both teams known for their technical prowess and strategic discipline. France's potent attack, led by Kylian Mbappé, will challenge Spain's possession-based game and defensive organization. The midfield battle will be crucial in determining control and creating scoring opportunities.

items.headline: Second Semifinal Spot Awaits Argentina vs. Switzerland Winner
items.body: England has advanced to the semifinals and will face the winner of the Quarterfinal match between Argentina and Switzerland. This match is scheduled to kick off at 01:00 UTC on July 12, 2026, at Arrowhead Stadium in Kansas City, Missouri, and its result is not yet available for post-match analysis at the current time.

metadata.venue: Arrowhead Stadium, Kansas City, Missouri, USA
